task.description: WF-02 Step 2c (SECURITY-REVIEWER hard gate) for REQ-037 on branch feature/WF02-REQ-037. Independently re-verify security-invariants.md S2/S3/S8, AC9 (bot never messages invitee), the tg_id=NULL path, code-generation entropy reuse (S4), and zero schema/migration change against the diff, not against BACKEND-DEV/REVIEWER's reports.

result.summary:
PASS. Re-derived independently from the diff (git diff master...HEAD) and GitHub issue #69's 10 ACs, not from BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's summaries.

S2 -- authorization, three negative cases:
apps/bot/src/handlers/inviteCodes.ts's resolveEventForIssuing() (used by all three issue handlers) and the list/detail handlers all call requireOrganizerForChapter(db, tgId, event.chapterId) -- domain/eventAuthorization.ts -- BEFORE any invite_codes read/write. This function is UNCHANGED by this diff (git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts is empty). Its branches, re-read directly (eventAuthorization.ts:60-78):
  (a) member: role==='member' -> {ok:false, reason:'not-organizer'}, refused before any INSERT. Diff never queries event_staff to grant an exception, so an EventStaff row does not change this outcome.
  (b) EventStaff member: EventStaff is a wholly separate table (event_staff, keyed eventId+userId, domain/eventStaff.ts) never joined or read anywhere in inviteCodes.ts/inviteCode.ts. Authorization is decided solely from users.role, so an EventStaff member (role still 'member') hits the identical 'not-organizer' branch as (a).
  (c) organizer of chapter A on chapter B's event: role==='organizer', chapterId!==targetChapterId -> {ok:false, reason:'wrong-chapter'} (eventAuthorization.ts:74-75), refused before any INSERT.
All three branches are pre-existing and already unit-tested at the pure-predicate level (domain/eventAuthorization.test.ts, all 6 cases including member/wrong-chapter/null-chapter, unchanged by this diff). Since checkOrganizerForChapter/requireOrganizerForChapter are untouched and are invoked strictly before every write and every read in inviteCodes.ts (verified by reading resolveEventForIssuing lines 92-128 and both the list handler lines 305-317 and the detail-callback handler lines 370-386), the three negative cases hold by composition: no code path reaches db.insert(inviteCodes) or a redeemer read without first clearing this check. No new invite_codes row is created on any of the three refusal paths because issuePersonalInviteCode/issueBulkInviteCode/issueCompanionInviteCode are only called after resolveEventForIssuing returns ok:true (handlers/inviteCodes.ts:151-171, 198-212, 239-259) -- there is no call site that reaches the INSERT before authorization.

S3 -- no phone/email leak, verified by reading the SQL myself:
listInviteCodeRedeemers's select clause (domain/inviteCode.ts:434-441): `registrationId, profiles.firstName, profiles.lastName, users.tgUsername, profiles.company` -- read directly, not paraphrased. No `profiles.phone`, no `profiles.email` token appears anywhere in this file. This is a structural exclusion (the columns are never named in the select), matching the same shape listPendingRequestsForOrganizer/listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin already use elsewhere in the codebase -- confirmed by pattern, not merely asserted by the design doc.

S8 -- audit, one row per issue, same transaction:
All three issue-* functions (domain/inviteCode.ts:175-314) run identically: `db.transaction(async (tx) => { ...insert into inviteCodes via tx...; await writeAuditLog(tx, {...}); return ...})`. writeAuditLog is called with `tx` (the transaction handle), not `db`, in every one of the three functions -- confirmed by reading each call site. action='invite_code.issue', entity='invite_code', entityId=the new row's id, actorUserId=the authorized organizer's users.id (from requireOrganizerForChapter's result, never the target/host id), payload carries only ids/eventId/shape/maxUses -- no phone/email/name (S11-safe). No AuditLog call exists on any refusal path (every refusal in resolveEventForIssuing/per-command validation returns before an issue-* function is ever invoked) -- exactly-once, never-on-refusal, transactionally atomic with the insert.

AC9 -- bot never messages the invitee, independently traced (not trusting REVIEWER's grep):
Ran my own search over the full diff for any outbound-messaging call. handlers/inviteCodes.ts contains exactly the following outbound calls, all traced individually: `ctx.reply(...)` in makeInvitePersonalHandler/makeInviteBulkHandler/makeInviteCompanionHandler/makeInviteCodesListHandler (targets ctx -- the invoking organizer's own chat, grammY's ctx.reply always replies into the chat the update came from) and `ctx.answerCallbackQuery(...)`/`ctx.reply(...)` in makeInviteCodeDetailCallbackHandler (same -- answers/replies into the callback's own originating chat). None of these calls take a chat_id/user_id argument at all (ctx.reply has no recipient parameter -- it is bound to the incoming update's chat by construction), so there is no code path by which issuedToUserId, grantsCompanionOf, or hostUserId's tg_id could be the recipient. Grepped domain/inviteCode.ts separately: it contains zero grammY/ctx/bot.api/sendMessage references at all (confirmed no import of grammy or any Context/Bot type in that file) -- the domain layer cannot message anyone, structurally. No second recipient exists anywhere in this diff. The link/code shown to the organizer (buildIssuedReply, handlers/inviteCodes.ts:74-77) is composed only from the bot username (already-resolved at process start) and the generated code string -- confirmed no PII (no name, phone, email, or any user-identifying field) is interpolated into `issuedReply`; the only variables are {code} and {link}, both derived solely from the invite_codes row itself. AC9 holds.

tg_id=NULL path: userExistsById (domain/user.ts:178-181) is `select id from users where id = userId limit 1` -- no reference to tgId anywhere in the function or its call sites (handlers/inviteCodes.ts:157, 245). issuePersonalInviteCode/issueCompanionInviteCode (domain/inviteCode.ts:175-222, 270-314) never read or reference tgId either -- the INSERT only uses targetUserId/hostUserId as opaque users.id foreign keys. No code in the issue path dereferences a `.tgId` field or assumes it is non-null; a user row with tgId=NULL flows through identically to one with tgId set. No crash/exception risk found.

S4 -- code-generation entropy, confirmed reused unchanged (not re-derived): diffed apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts against master byte-for-byte for lines 1-38 (INVITE_CODE_ALPHABET, INVITE_CODE_LENGTH, generateInviteCode()) -- IDENTICAL, zero changes. This diff is purely additive after line 38; no new code-generation function, no second alphabet, no wrapper around generateInviteCode() exists anywhere in the diff. Confirmed via `diff <(git show master:apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts) <(git show HEAD:apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts)`.

Schema/migration: `git diff master...HEAD --stat` lists no file under apps/bot/src/db/ or any drizzle migrations directory. Zero schema change confirmed independently.

No new PII exposure via shareable link: covered under AC9 above -- the ?start=i_<code> link and bare code shown to the organizer encode only the generated code string, nothing else.
issues: N/A items: S1 (consent) not touched -- this diff writes no User/Profile row and records no new consent; S5-S7, S9-S10, S12-S14 do not apply -- this diff touches no check-in flow, no notification scheduler, no broadcast, no export, no deletion, and no publication surface. Reason for each N/A: the diff's write surface is limited to one invite_codes INSERT + one AuditLog INSERT per issuing command, and its read surface is limited to invite_codes/registrations/profiles/users SELECTs already covered under S3 above -- no other invariant's subject matter (checked-in state, capacity, notifications, marketing sends, plaintext logging, CSV export, deletion, speaker publication) is written or read anywhere in this diff.

CARRIED FORWARD (not this gate's to resolve, already flagged by REVIEWER): i18n catalog strings are provisional pending CONTENT-BA/product-owner wording; REQ-033 §6's re-issuance/chunking open questions remain unresolved per design's own explicit non-resolution.
